items.title: Ann Rabson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 21, 2007
items.q: Little Richard once, I was playing at a thing in L.A. with Saffire. And he came up to me. ... he came up afterward and said, “I really like your piano playing.”

ctx.x: Were your tastes usually not aligned with the kids who were your age?

Absolutely. Absolutely. When I was in seventh grade they dubbed me “Jazzbo,” and they made fun of me. Well I loved jazz. I’ve always, I still love jazz. And I was listening to bop. I mean I was just really into that. But I was also, you know I was very lucky because the popular music when I was coming up was pretty cool, some of it. And I really loved Bo Diddley and Little Richard and you know people like that, Ruth Brown.
Were you a word person when you listened to the music? Did you really pay attention to the words?
